C0001.description:
The regex the spec mandates at `bench/BUILD_BOT_TEST_BENCH_FIX_SPEC.md:35` carries `(?:
|$)` after the stop-label colon. This makes the stop lookahead fire *only* when a section label is followed by a newline or EOF — so a label with content on the same line is not recognised as a boundary, and the preceding section swallows it. Executed evidence, extracting the spec's own code block out of the real spec file and running it:
INITIAL_ANSWER: 42
ISSUES_FOUND: none
REVISED_ANSWER: 43
  spec code  -> INITIAL_ANSWER = '42
ISSUES_FOUND: none
REVISED_ANSWER: 43'   # leaked
  shipped    -> INITIAL_ANSWER = '42'                                            # correct
`run_benchmark.py:818-821` documents the identical defect by name: *"EPP M1 fix 1: removed `(?:
|$)` after colon — models often put content on the same line as the label … causing section leakage."*

```python
def _extract_section(text: str, label: str) -> str | None:
```

C0002.description:
Two coupled defects on the case-variance path.
*(a) Spec side:* the prescribed `_extract_section` (spec lines 32-44) uses `re.DOTALL` only and matches labels literally. The shipped function uses `re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE` plus title-case stop variants, attributed to *"Gemini R2 fix 6: LLMs frequently vary case (e.g. 'Revised Answer:' vs 'REVISED_ANSWER:')"* (`run_benchmark.py:799-802`). The spec states no such requirement, so literal re-application drops it.
*(b) Implementation side:* the shipped code's own fix is dead. `run_benchmark.py:827` is `re.escape(label).replace(r"\_", r"[_ ]")`. Since Python 3.7 `re.escape` does not escape `_`, so `re.escape("REVISED_ANSWER") == "REVISED_ANSWER"` — the literal `\_` never occurs and `replace` is a no-op. Executed:
re.escape('REVISED_ANSWER')                         -> 'REVISED_ANSWER'
.replace(r'\_', r'[_ ]')                            -> 'REVISED_ANSWER'   # unchanged
shipped _extract_section("Revised Answer:\n43\n")   -> None
The *stop*-label title variant at lines 811-814 is built independently of `re.escape` and does work. So the function can stop at `Revised Answer:` but cannot find it — an asymmetry that returns `None` for every section of a title-case response.

```python
def _extract_section(text: str, label: str) -> str | None:
```

```python
def _extract_section(text: str, label: str) -> str | None:
    stop_labels = [re.escape(item) for item in SECTION_LABELS if item != label]
    if stop_labels:
        stop_pattern = rf"(?=\n(?:{'|'.join(stop_labels)}):\s*(?:\n|$)|\Z)"

    pattern = rf"(?:^|\n){re.escape(label)}:\s*\n?(.*?){stop_pattern}"
```

`BUILD_BOT_TEST_BENCH_FIX_SPEC.md:35` mandates a stop pattern whose `(?:\n|$)` clause makes section-boundary detection fail whenever a label carries content on the same line:
stop_pattern = rf"(?=\n(?:{'|'.join(stop_labels)}):\s*(?:\n|$)|\Z)"
`\s*` consumes the space after `ISSUES_FOUND:`, then `(?:\n|$)` demands a newline or EOF but meets `U` of "Units" — the lookahead fails, no stop fires. I executed the spec's function verbatim on `INITIAL_ANSWER: d1\nISSUES_FOUND: i1\nREVISED_ANSWER: r1`:

| label | spec regex extracts |
|---|---|
| `INITIAL_ANSWER` | `'d1\nISSUES_FOUND: i1\nREVISED_ANSWER: r1'` |
| `ISSUES_FOUND` | `'i1\nREVISED_ANSWER: r1'` |
| `REVISED_ANSWER` | `'r1'` |

`INITIAL_ANSWER` swallows the entire response. The shipped code produces `'d1'`, `'i1'`, `'r1'` correctly, because `run_benchmark.py:821` already removed exactly this `(?:\n|$)` — its comment states the old pattern was "causing section leakage".

```python
def _extract_section(text: str, label: str) -> str | None:
```
```python
    def label_pattern(item: str) -> str:
        # Tolerate the separator and case variants models actually emit:
        # "REVISED_ANSWER", "REVISED ANSWER", "Revised Answer", "revised_answer".
        return r"[_ ]".join(re.escape(part) for part in item.split("_"))

    stop_labels = [label_pattern(item) for item in SECTION_LABELS if item != label]
```

| Trigger corpus | Spec-mandated result | Shipped result (`run_benchmark.py:796-833`) |
|---|---|---|
| `INITIAL_ANSWER: Paris.
ISSUES_FOUND: - terse
REVISED_ANSWER: Paris, France.` | `'Paris.

REVISED_ANSWER: Paris, France.'` | `'Paris.'` |

- terse'` | `'Paris.'` |
| `ISSUES_FOUND:

REVISED_ANSWER:
Paris, France.` | leaks | also leaks → `'REVISED_ANSWER:
Paris, France.'` |

Root causes, in order:
1. `(?:
|$)` after the stop label (spec line 35). Requires a stop label to be followed by a newline or EOF, so a label with content on the same line is not recognised as a stop. The shipped code deleted this suffix deliberately; the in-code comment at `run_benchmark.py:818-821` reads *"EPP M1 fix 1: removed `(?:
|$)` after colon — models often put content on the same line as the label... causing section leakage."* The spec mandates putting it back.

?` in the opener (spec line 39) — `\s*` is greedy and swallows the newline that the stop-lookahead requires as its anchor, so an empty section captures the *next* section's body. def _extract_section(text: str, label: str) -> str | None:
```python
    # Stop labels are matched case-insensitively and in title-case form too,
    # because models write "Issues Found:" as readily as "ISSUES_FOUND:".
    stop_labels = []
    for item in SECTION_LABELS:
        if item != label:
            escaped = re.escape(item)
            title_variant = re.escape(item.replace("_", " ").title())
            stop_labels.append(escaped)
            if title_variant != escaped:
                stop_labels.append(title_variant)

    if stop_labels:
        # Do NOT require (?:\n|$) after the stop label's colon: models often put
        # content on the same line ("ISSUES_FOUND: - terse"), and demanding a
        # newline or EOF there makes such a label invisible as a stop, leaking
        # every following section into this one.
        stop_pattern = rf"(?=\n(?:{'|'.join(stop_labels)}):\s*|\Z)"
    else:
        stop_pattern = r"\Z"

    label_pattern = re.escape(label).replace(r"\_", r"[_ ]")
    pattern = rf"(?:^|\n){label_pattern}:\s*\n?(.*?){stop_pattern}"
    match = re.search(pattern, text, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
    if not match:
        return None
    value = match.group(1).strip()
    return value or None
```

m3 = re.search(r'^### 3\) `bench/report\.py`', text, re.M)

mC = re.search(r'^#### C\.', sec2, re.M)

assert '`estimated_p`' in body, "2C no longer names estimated_p"

    r'denominator', r'at[-_ ]risk', r'chain[-_ ]length', r'passes[-_ ]run',
    r'passes[-_ ]completed', r'passes[-_ ]executed', r'reached pass',
    r'eligible', r'surviv', r'censor',

print(f"denominator vocabulary anywhere : {hits_whole or 'NONE'}")

print(f"at-risk denominator curve {[round(v,3) for v in a]} -> estimated_p={pa:.3f}")

§2C (`:85-87`) recognises exactly one fit-failure category — *"If fitting is unavailable/fails"* — and §3C (`:99-100`) recognises exactly one degradation — *"If `estimated_p` or `r_squared` is missing"*. fit = {'estimated_p': 0.2902, 'r_squared': 1.0,
       'fitted_values': [0.2902, 0.496184, 0.642392]}
max |residual| = 0.2098

  Estimated p:  0.2902
  R-squared:    1.0000
  Model:        C(n) = 1 - (1 - 0.2902)^n

    C( 1) = 0.290   C( 3) = 0.642   C( 5) = 0.820   C(10) = 0.968

The placebo baseline arm is confounded on two variables, and the spec forbids neither. `bench/run_benchmark.py:1692` `run_placebo()` does not route to `run_experimental()`; it delegates to `run_adaptive()` (`:1701`), which carries CC+CX confer early termination (`:1618`, `if i >= confer_after:`, `confer_after=3`). `run_experimental()` has no `break` in its pass loop — it runs the full count. Executed with every provider and the confer CLI stubbed:
--passes 2: standard=2 placebo=2  starved=False
--passes 3: standard=3 placebo=3  starved=False
--passes 4: standard=4 placebo=3  starved=True
--passes 5: standard=5 placebo=3  starved=True
`evaluate.py:380-402` marks `experimental_detected=True` if any pass detects the fault. Detection is cumulative over passes. A baseline given 3 passes against an arm given 5 is given fewer chances to detect, and the deficit lands in `control_vs_experimental.detection_rate_lift` — the benchmark's headline number — in the direction that flatters the CDSFL hypothesis.

Second confound on the same mechanism: at `--passes 3` the placebo arm makes 1 confer call (two CLI invocations) that the CDSFL arm never makes. Third: `run_adaptive` stamps `condition: "experimental_adaptive"` (`:1672`), so a `placebo` record and an `adaptive` record are byte-indistinguishable at the record level.
